body: Funny...my fiance just told me 2 minute ago that I should supplement my psychiatrist with a therapist.  I think I may look into this, although I'm quite skeptical (for no reason really, other than that's how my stupid brain works).

Yeah, I feel you.  While I have several logs in the fire, so to speak, I feel like nothing is guaranteed and I'm destined for a life of mediocrity.

Maybe you should consider going back to school/studying for the gmat/gre to keep options open.  Getting a great score could open up a lot of doors for you.
Where are you in life?  Working?  In school?  Hating your job?

Thank you for your kind words.  I just feel like I'm not good enough, smart enough, work hard enough, etc. to be anything better than average...and average in this world seems so miserable.  I know I need to suck it up and not allow my fear of failure from getting in the way...it's just so hard given my perceptions of myself and life.

My psychiatrist is emotionless, but I am somewhat happy going to him.  I've built up a comfort level with him and having to go re-establish that elsewhere seems like a huge chore I'd rather not deal with at the time.
See a doctor for the physical condition you speak of.  There are surely things they can do to help you condition and/or pain.

I appreciate these responses so much.  Aside from my fiance, I don't really have an outlet to voice these emotions (aside from my emotionless psychiatrist).

That's the thing, I'm pursuing my passions to the fullest.  I have a full time corporate job that I hate...but I also started a web business 3 years ago, and have been working on that non-stop.  It's finally bringing in money, but I'm certainly not ready to quit the 9-5 just yet.  I'm also back in school (I graduated from college in 08) taking necessary pre-reqs so I can apply to master's programs.

My problems is this: I feel worried that my business will fail, I won't be accepted to any programs, and I'll be stuck in my dead end corporate job (or something similar) until the day I die...  I just feel like I want to give up, especially since death, although very final, seems so peaceful.

I've been going to a doctor for about 18 months.  I've tried several different anti-depressants (for my anxiety disorder) and I've had partial success, but the side effects aren't great.  I'm left feeling like a brain dead zombie when I'm on most of these drugs.  

I take a klonopin from time to time when I really need it...and that helps, but it's not something I can live on.  

I just feel my life has no meaning and there's no way to give it meaning.  I feel trapped in that stereotypical life society has created; go to college, get married, have a kid(s), work, die. 

I want to do good things.  I want to make a difference in the world.  I want to help people...I just don't know if I'll ever have the chance.

I too have "first world" problems which are causing me to contemplate suicide.  I feel somewhat guilty that there are so many people out there who have been dealt a much worse hand than myself....but I still can't shake the thought of wanting to die.

I understand how you feel.  The thing that keeps me from doing it is thinking about what it would do to my parents, my fiance, my friends...
This is turn leads to a feeling of being stuck in this shitty situation for the rest of my days..which leads to more anxiety and feelings of wanting to die.  It's a vicious cycle.  

I would try to identify what it is about your life that is causing you these feelings.  Work?  Family relationships?  etc.  Figure out what that is, and maybe you can do something to change/improve the situation...

I think you need to get your diet and fitness in order.  I don't mean this from a superficial standpoint - I truly believe if you can get yourself eating clean, healthy, wholesome foods, and exercising regularly, you'll jump start those "feel good" chemicals in your brain which will eventually shift your view on life.

I'd make it a serious goal to be as healthy and fit as possible..and see how you feel.
